An unusually light day for AI research, with only two substantive original contributions. The standout is a novel AI-assisted policy analysis using Claude Sonnet 4.5 with web search to systematically catalog every US congressperson's public AGI positions—producing actionable governance data.

  • A philosophical piece on AI safety argues that flourishing-focused interventions may dominate survival-focused ones even under high existential risk scenarios, using mathematical framing
  • AISC project update on 'Understanding Trust' references an IQA paper output from Spring 2025 cohort work
  • MATS Summer 2026 applications closing January 18th—relevant for safety talent pipeline but not research itself

Remaining items cover unrelated topics: neuroscience on stuttering therapy, economic analysis of Japan's debt position, job postings, and satirical essays. No technical ML papers or architecture advances appeared today.

entry.title: What Washington Says About AGI

author.name: zroe1

entry.summary: Original research using Claude Sonnet 4.5 with web search to systematically analyze every US congressperson's public statements on AI. Findings show AGI awareness is not partisan but is rare, with x-risk concerns and US-China competition focus also mapped against ideology.

entry.title: Focusing on Flourishing Even When Survival is Unlikely (I)

author.name: Cleo Nardo

entry.summary: Philosophical argument that even when existential risk is very high (e.g., 99%), interventions focused on improving the quality of post-survival futures ('flourishing') may have higher expected value than survival-focused interventions. References Will MacAskill's August 2025 work 'Better Futures.'

entry.title: Applying to MATS: What the Program Is Like, and Who It’s For

author.name: Raj Thimmiah

entry.summary: Detailed information about the MATS (ML Alignment Theory Scholars) Summer 2026 program with applications closing January 18, 2026. Describes program structure, mentorship model, and success metrics for prospective AI safety researchers.

entry.title: Understanding Trust: Project Update

author.name: abramdemski

entry.summary: Project update from abramdemski on his AISC (AI Safety Camp) project about 'Understanding Trust,' which ran in Spring 2025 with four mentees. The project produced a co-authored ILIAD 2024 paper and recorded videos explaining the research agenda are being uploaded.

entry.title: Turning Down the Overthinking: How Cathodal Brain Stimulation Could Transform Stuttering Therapy

author.name: Rudaiba

entry.summary: Neuroscience exploration of how cathodal brain stimulation might help stuttering by reducing conscious interference with automatic speech processes. Based on the 'reinvestment hypothesis' that conscious attention can impair motor skills that should be automatic.

entry.title: The truth behind the 2026 J.P. Morgan Healthcare Conference

author.name: Abhishaike Mahajan

entry.summary: Satirical essay drawing parallels between Athanasius Kircher's speculative 1654 geography 'Mundus Subterraneus' and the author's experience at the 2026 J.P. Morgan Healthcare Conference. Commentary on the nature of secondhand knowledge and conferences.

entry.title: Lightcone is hiring a generalist, a designer, and a campus operations co-lead

author.name: habryka

entry.summary: Job posting from Lightcone (LessWrong operators) for three positions: senior designer, campus manager, and core team generalist. Discusses organizational values around design quality and truth-seeking.

entry.title: Japan is a bank

author.name: bhauth

entry.summary: Economic analysis comparing Japan's debt/GDP ratio to the US, arguing that when accounting for government-held assets, Japan's net debt position isn't as alarming as headline figures suggest, and the US situation is more comparable than typically assumed.

entry.title: Forfeiting Ill-Gotten Gains

author.name: jefftk

entry.summary: Parenting principle about enforcement: when punishing rule-breaking, the combination of penalty and forfeiture of gains must leave the violator worse off than if they hadn't broken the rule. Extended briefly to crime deterrence principles.

entry.title: Research Summary: January 17, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research centers on AI economics, model evaluation, and safety frameworks. A large-scale study with 500+ professionals and 13 LLMs establishes scaling laws for economic impact, finding each year of frontier progress reduces task completion time by measurable margins.

  • Future-as-Label introduces self-supervised training using temporal outcomes from real-world data streams, eliminating costly human annotation
  • Mechanistic interpretability work reveals models may exhibit fixed biases rather than genuine reasoning on inductive tasks
  • Revealed preference methodology applied across GPT-5.1, Claude-Opus-4.5, and other frontier models to elicit trained character traits

Safety contributions include a technical framework for prioritizing net-sabotage-value vulnerabilities in AI control, plus analysis reframing persuasion risk from adversarial to trusted advisor threat models. Historical precedent mapping for 13 ASI failure modes provides grounding for unprecedented risk scenarios.

entry.title: Scaling Laws for Economic Impacts: Experimental Evidence from 500 Professionals and 13 LLMs

author.name: Ali Merali

entry.summary: Experimental study with 500+ professionals testing 13 LLMs of varying compute levels on real tasks. Finds each year of frontier progress reduces task completion time by ~8% (56% from compute scaling, 44% algorithmic). Key puzzle: human-AI collaborative output quality stays flat despite improving models, suggesting users cap realized gains.

entry.title: Future-as-Label: Scalable Supervision from Real-World Outcomes

author.name: Ben Turtel

entry.summary: Introduces 'Future-as-Label' training methodology that uses temporal outcomes from real-world data streams as supervision signal, eliminating need for human annotation. Fine-tuning Qwen3-32B on historical news improved Brier score by 27% and halved calibration error, outperforming the 7× larger Qwen3-235B on Metaculus forecasting questions.

entry.title: Eliciting Frontier Model Character Training

author.name: avikrishna

entry.summary: Systematic study applying revealed preference methods to elicit personality/character traits across all major frontier models (including GPT-5.1, Claude, Gemini-3). Uses external judge models rather than self-reporting, measuring 144 traits and finding consistent top-trait preferences across models but divergence in lower-ranked traits.

entry.title: Is It Reasoning or Just a Fixed Bias?

author.name: Sriram Kiron

entry.summary: Mechanistic interpretability study investigating whether LLMs actually reason on inductive/abductive tasks or exhibit fixed biases. Finds models have a consistent generalization tendency (outputting parent concepts regardless of task requirements) with 1-hop and 2-hop accuracies summing to ~100%, suggesting models aren't performing genuine reasoning but applying fixed heuristics.

entry.title: Should control down-weight negative net-sabotage-value threats?

author.name: Fabien Roger

entry.summary: Technical AI control post arguing that when prioritizing vulnerability mitigation, one should focus on vulnerabilities with positive 'net-sabotage-value' from a scheming AI's perspective, and down-weight those where being caught would cost the AI more than the damage caused.

entry.title: Powerful misaligned AIs may be extremely persuasive, especially absent mitigations

author.name: Cody Rushing

entry.summary: Analysis of persuasion risks from misaligned AI, reframing from adversarial (salesman) model to trusted advisor model where users have strong incentives to believe AI. Emphasizes large attack surface (personal data, social media, information environment) and competitive disadvantages of being skeptical.

entry.title: Digital Minds: A Quickstart Guide

author.name: Avi Parrack

entry.summary: Introductory guide to the ethical and policy considerations around digital minds, covering uncertainty about AI consciousness, risks of under/over-attributing moral status, and current research directions. Notes majority of experts estimate >50% chance of subjective AI experience by 2050.

entry.title: Precedents for the Unprecedented: Historical Analogies for Thirteen Artificial Superintelligence Risks

author.name: James_Miller

entry.summary: Catalogs thirteen potential ASI failure modes paired with historical precedents that demonstrate similar patterns, arguing that superintelligence risks are extensions of observable failure modes rather than speculative. Written with extensive AI assistance.

entry.title: [Pre-print] Building safe AGI as an ergonomics problem

author.name: ricardotkcl

entry.summary: Pre-print framing AGI safety through ergonomics/human factors lens, arguing for applying established safety engineering principles to AI development. Submitted to ergonomics journal but rejected after peer review.

entry.title: Why falling labor share ≠ falling employment

author.name: Lydia Nottingham

entry.summary: Economic analysis arguing that AI increasing the share of total work done by machines doesn't necessitate declining human employment, drawing on concepts of complementarity between human and AI labor and historical precedents.

entry.title: The culture and design of human-AI interactions

author.name: zef

entry.summary: Reflective commentary on evolving human-AI interaction patterns, noting that power accrues to those understanding capability shifts, AI increases variance, and education quality may become more uneven as people outsource detailed engagement to AI.

entry.title: Monthly Roundup #38: January 2026

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's monthly aggregation covering California policy (wealth tax causing tech exodus), economic observations, and various topics. Not focused on AI research specifically.

entry.title: Total utilitarianism is fine

author.name: Abhimanyu Pallavi Sudhir

entry.summary: Philosophical argument defending total utilitarianism against common objections, using formal notation to clarify assumptions about aggregating welfare across agents.

entry.title: Comparing yourself to other people

author.name: dominicq

entry.summary: Philosophical reflection on social comparison being inherently local rather than historical or global, arguing that comparing modern living standards to historical averages misses the functional purpose of comparison for motivating action.

entry.title: Confession: I pranked Inkhaven to make sure no one fails

author.name: Mikhail Samin

entry.summary: Personal story about pranking a writing challenge (Inkhaven) by secretly editing participants' posts to ensure no one failed, with tangential references to quantum immortality and anthropics.

entry.title: How to Use Foam Earplugs Correctly

author.name: Morpheus

entry.summary: Practical guide explaining that foam earplugs need to be rolled before insertion for proper fit.

entry.title: The Default Contra Dance Weekend Deal

author.name: jefftk

entry.summary: Documentation of typical arrangements for contra dance weekend events, covering scheduling, performer compensation, and organizational norms.

entry.title: Research Summary: January 16, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research features critical safety evaluations and theoretical breakthroughs. A unified safety report benchmarks GPT-5.2, Gemini 3 Pro, Grok 4.1 Fast, and four other frontier models across standardized safety dimensions. OpenRouter's 100+ trillion token empirical study provides unprecedented insights into real-world LLM usage patterns.

  • Molmo2 releases open weights for video-language understanding with point-driven grounding, advancing open-source multimodal capabilities
  • Theoretical work reveals neural scaling laws emerge from random graph walks without power-law structure, challenging prevailing assumptions
  • Alignment Pretraining demonstrates AI discourse in training corpora causally produces self-fulfilling (mis)alignment outcomes
  • CaMeLs introduces architectural isolation defenses for computer use agents against prompt injection via single-shot planning

Mechanistic analysis reveals Hierarchical Reasoning Models exhibit "guessing shortcuts" and fail on simple puzzles violating fixed-point assumptions. ML-Master 2.0 enables ultra-long-horizon autonomous ML engineering spanning days/weeks through cognitive accumulation. A novel proof connects transformer attention to tropical polynomial circuits (max-plus algebra), revealing forward passes as shortest-path computations.

entry.title: A Safety Report on GPT-5.2, Gemini 3 Pro, Qwen3-VL, Doubao 1.8, Grok 4.1 Fast, Nano Banana Pro, and Seedream 4.5

author.name: Xingjun Ma, Yixu Wang, Hengyuan Xu, Yutao Wu, Yifan Ding, Yunhan Zhao, Zilong Wang, Jiabin Hua, Ming Wen, Jianan Liu, Ranjie Duan, Yifeng Gao, Yingshui Tan, Yunhao Chen, Hui Xue, Xin Wang, Wei Cheng, Jingjing Chen, Zuxuan Wu, Bo Li, Yu-Gang Jiang

entry.summary: Comprehensive safety evaluation of 7 frontier models: GPT-5.2, Gemini 3 Pro, Qwen3-VL, Doubao 1.8, Grok 4.1 Fast, Nano Banana Pro, and Seedream 4.5 across language, vision-language, and image generation using unified protocol.

entry.title: State of AI: An Empirical 100 Trillion Token Study with OpenRouter

author.name: Malika Aubakirova, Alex Atallah, Chris Clark, Justin Summerville, Anjney Midha

entry.summary: Large-scale empirical analysis of 100+ trillion tokens of real-world LLM usage through OpenRouter platform. Studies usage patterns across tasks, geographies, time, and the shift to reasoning models following o1's release.

entry.title: Molmo2: Open Weights and Data for Vision-Language Models with Video Understanding and Grounding

author.name: Christopher Clark, Jieyu Zhang, Zixian Ma, Jae Sung Park, Mohammadreza Salehi, Rohun Tripathi, Sangho Lee, Zhongzheng Ren, Chris Dongjoo Kim, Yinuo Yang, Vincent Shao, Yue Yang, Weikai Huang, Ziqi Gao, Taira Anderson, Jianrui Zhang, Jitesh Jain, George Stoica, Winson Han, Ali Farhadi, Ranjay Krishna

entry.summary: Releases Molmo2, a state-of-the-art open-source VLM family with video understanding and point-driven grounding capabilities. Provides complete open weights and training data, addressing lack of transparency in the field.

entry.title: Toward Ultra-Long-Horizon Agentic Science: Cognitive Accumulation for Machine Learning Engineering

author.name: Xinyu Zhu, Yuzhu Cai, Zexi Liu, Bingyang Zheng, Cheng Wang, Rui Ye, Jiaao Chen, Hanrui Wang, Wei-Chen Wang, Yuzhi Zhang, Linfeng Zhang, Weinan E, Di Jin, Siheng Chen

entry.summary: Presents ML-Master 2.0, an autonomous agent for ultra-long-horizon ML engineering tasks spanning days/weeks. Reframes context management as cognitive accumulation to handle sparse feedback over extended periods.

entry.title: CaMeLs Can Use Computers Too: System-level Security for Computer Use Agents

author.name: Hanna Foerster, Robert Mullins, Tom Blanchard, Nicolas Papernot, Kristina Nikoli\'c, Florian Tram\`er, Ilia Shumailov, Cheng Zhang, Yiren Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces architectural isolation defense for Computer Use Agents against prompt injection attacks via Single-Shot Planning. Demonstrates UI workflows are structurally predictable, enabling security through separating planning from observation.

entry.title: On the origin of neural scaling laws: from random graphs to natural language

author.name: Maissam Barkeshli, Alberto Alfarano, Andrey Gromov

entry.summary: Studies neural scaling laws using transformers trained on random walks on graphs, demonstrating scaling laws emerge even without power-law structure in data. Provides new theoretical perspective on scaling law origins.

entry.title: Evaluating Novelty in AI-Generated Research Plans Using Multi-Workflow LLM Pipelines

author.name: Devesh Saraogi, Rohit Singhee, Dhruv Kumar

entry.summary: Benchmarks 5 agentic workflows for research novelty including Reflection, Sakana AI v2, Google Co-Scientist, GPT Deep Research (GPT-5.1), and recursive decomposition. Investigates whether multi-step systems overcome 'smart plagiarism'.

entry.title: Alignment Pretraining: AI Discourse Causes Self-Fulfilling (Mis)alignment

author.name: Cameron Tice, Puria Radmard, Samuel Ratnam, Andy Kim, David Africa, Kyle O'Brien

entry.summary: Studies how AI discourse in pretraining corpora causally influences alignment outcomes. Training on misalignment discourse increases misaligned behavior while aligned discourse reduces it.

entry.title: The Geometry of Thought: Disclosing the Transformer as a Tropical Polynomial Circuit

author.name: Faruk Alpay, Bilge Senturk

entry.summary: Proves that transformer self-attention in high-confidence regime operates in the tropical semiring (max-plus algebra), revealing the forward pass executes dynamic programming (Bellman-Ford) on token similarity graphs.

entry.title: Breaking Up with Normatively Monolithic Agency with GRACE: A Reason-Based Neuro-Symbolic Architecture for Safe and Ethical AI Alignment

author.name: Felix Jahn, Yannic Muskalla, Lisa Dargasz, Patrick Schramowski, Kevin Baum

entry.summary: Introduces GRACE, a neuro-symbolic containment architecture decoupling normative reasoning from instrumental decision-making. Uses deontic logic-based Moral Module to constrain agent actions for safety and ethics.

entry.title: Thinking Long, but Short: Stable Sequential Test-Time Scaling for Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Michael R. Metel, Yufei Cui, Boxing Chen, Prasanna Parthasarathi

entry.summary: Presents Min-Seek, a novel test-time scaling method that stabilizes accuracy across varying reasoning lengths, addressing the accuracy degradation problem when models 'think longer'. Removes need for reasoning length fine-tuning while improving accuracy.

entry.title: Transition Matching Distillation for Fast Video Generation

author.name: Weili Nie, Julius Berner, Nanye Ma, Chao Liu, Saining Xie, Arash Vahdat

entry.summary: Presents Transition Matching Distillation (TMD) from NVIDIA for distilling video diffusion models into efficient few-step generators. Decomposes backbone into main component and lightweight conditional flow modules.

entry.title: Contextual StereoSet: Stress-Testing Bias Alignment Robustness in Large Language Models

author.name: Abhinaba Basu, Pavan Chakraborty

entry.summary: Demonstrates that LLM bias measurements shift dramatically when prompts include different contextual framing (time periods, audiences, social settings) without adversarial prompting. Finds up to 13 percentage point shifts in stereotype selection across 13 models.

entry.title: Are Your Reasoning Models Reasoning or Guessing? A Mechanistic Analysis of Hierarchical Reasoning Models

author.name: Zirui Ren, Ziming Liu

entry.summary: Mechanistic study of Hierarchical Reasoning Models revealing surprising failures: fail on simple puzzles violating fixed-point assumptions, exhibit 'grokking' dynamics with sudden accuracy jumps, and multiple fixed points causing guess-like behavior.

entry.title: Understanding and Preserving Safety in Fine-Tuned LLMs

author.name: Jiawen Zhang, Yangfan Hu, Kejia Chen, Lipeng He, Jiachen Ma, Jian Lou, Dan Li, Jian Liu, Xiaohu Yang, Ruoxi Jia

entry.summary: Studies fine-tuning safety degradation in LLMs from geometric perspective, finding safety- and utility-oriented gradients can be disentangled in parameter space for preserving alignment.

entry.title: TRIM: Hybrid Inference via Targeted Stepwise Routing in Multi-Step Reasoning Tasks

author.name: Vansh Kapoor, Aman Gupta, Hao Chen, Anurag Beniwal, Jing Huang, Aviral Kumar

entry.summary: Proposes TRIM for step-level routing in multi-step reasoning, directing only critical steps to larger models while smaller models handle routine continuations. Targets steps likely to cause cascading errors.

entry.title: Agent Skills in the Wild: An Empirical Study of Security Vulnerabilities at Scale

author.name: Yi Liu, Weizhe Wang, Ruitao Feng, Yao Zhang, Guangquan Xu, Gelei Deng, Yuekang Li, Leo Zhang

entry.summary: First large-scale security analysis of AI agent skill marketplaces, analyzing 42,447 skills with SkillScan. Finds 26.1% contain vulnerabilities spanning 14 distinct types.

entry.title: Discrete Feynman-Kac Correctors

author.name: Mohsin Hasan, Viktor Ohanesian, Artem Gazizov, Yoshua Bengio, Al\'an Aspuru-Guzik, Roberto Bondesan, Marta Skreta, Kirill Neklyudov

entry.summary: Introduces Discrete Feynman-Kac Correctors for controlling discrete masked diffusion models at inference via SMC algorithms, enabling temperature annealing, distribution guidance, and classifier-free guidance.

entry.title: Continuum Memory Architectures for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Joe Logan

entry.summary: Defines Continuum Memory Architecture (CMA), a class of systems maintaining and updating state across interactions through persistent storage, selective retention, associative routing, and temporal chaining. Addresses RAG's limitation of treating memory as stateless lookup.

entry.title: Sparse-RL: Breaking the Memory Wall in LLM Reinforcement Learning via Stable Sparse Rollouts

author.name: Sijia Luo, Xiaokang Zhang, Yuxuan Hu, Bohan Zhang, Ke Wang, Jinbo Su, Mengshu Sun, Lei Liang, Jing Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes Sparse-RL to address memory bottleneck in LLM reinforcement learning by enabling stable training under sparse KV cache rollouts. Identifies and addresses policy mismatch problem in sparse RL.

entry.title: ReasAlign: Reasoning Enhanced Safety Alignment against Prompt Injection Attack

author.name: Hao Li, Yankai Yang, G. Edward Suh, Ning Zhang, Chaowei Xiao

entry.summary: Presents ReasAlign, a model-level defense against indirect prompt injection attacks in LLM agents using structured reasoning to analyze queries, detect conflicts, and preserve task continuity.

entry.title: High-accuracy and dimension-free sampling with diffusions

author.name: Khashayar Gatmiry, Sitan Chen, Adil Salim

entry.summary: Proposes new diffusion model solver achieving dimension-free iteration complexity for high-accuracy sampling, using interplay between low-degree approximation and collocation method.

entry.title: Inference-time Physics Alignment of Video Generative Models with Latent World Models

author.name: Jianhao Yuan, Xiaofeng Zhang, Felix Friedrich, Nicolas Beltran-Velez, Melissa Hall, Reyhane Askari-Hemmat, Xiaochuang Han, Nicolas Ballas, Michal Drozdzal, Adriana Romero-Soriano

entry.summary: Introduces WMReward, using VJEPA-2 latent world model as a reward signal to guide video generation toward physics plausibility at inference time. Treats physics alignment as inference-time problem rather than training issue.

entry.title: Defending Large Language Models Against Jailbreak Attacks via In-Decoding Safety-Awareness Probing

author.name: Yinzhi Zhao, Ming Wang, Shi Feng, Xiaocui Yang, Daling Wang, Yifei Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes in-decoding defense against jailbreaks by probing latent safety signals during generation. Observes that even jailbroken models exhibit internal safety signals that get overridden, enabling intervention.

entry.title: Unlabeled Data Can Provably Enhance In-Context Learning of Transformers

author.name: Renpu Liu, Jing Yang

entry.summary: Proves that unlabeled data with chain-of-thought prompting can provably enhance in-context learning for multi-class linear classification, with multi-layer transformers reducing labeling costs.

entry.title: Syntactic Framing Fragility: An Audit of Robustness in LLM Ethical Decisions

author.name: Katherine Elkins, Jon Chun

entry.summary: Introduces Syntactic Framing Fragility framework to audit whether LLMs maintain consistent ethical judgments across logically equivalent but syntactically different prompts. Tests 23 models including US and Chinese systems.

entry.title: The Algorithmic Gaze: An Audit and Ethnography of the LAION-Aesthetics Predictor Model

author.name: Jordan Taylor, William Agnew, Maarten Sap, Sarah E. Fox, Haiyi Zhu

entry.summary: Audits LAION Aesthetic Predictor (LAP) used to curate Stable Diffusion training data. Examines 1.2B images filtered by LAP and conducts ethnographic study to understand whose aesthetic preferences are encoded.

entry.title: PRL: Process Reward Learning Improves LLMs' Reasoning Ability and Broadens the Reasoning Boundary

author.name: Jiarui Yao, Ruida Wang, Tong Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes Process Reward Learning (PRL) decomposing entropy-regularized RL into process-level signals for LLM reasoning without needing MCTS or separate reward models. Provides theoretical grounding.

entry.title: Antisocial behavior towards large language model users: experimental evidence

author.name: Pawe{\l} Niszczota, Cassandra Gr\"utzner

entry.summary: Experimental study (N=491) showing people engage in costly punishment of LLM users, destroying 36% of earnings from those who relied exclusively on AI. Punishment increases monotonically with actual LLM use, revealing significant antisocial responses to AI assistance.

entry.title: LLMdoctor: Token-Level Flow-Guided Preference Optimization for Efficient Test-Time Alignment of Large Language Models

author.name: Tiesunlong Shen, Rui Mao, Jin Wang, Heming Sun, Jian Zhang, Xuejie Zhang, Erik Cambria

entry.summary: Introduces LLMdoctor for efficient test-time alignment using a patient-doctor paradigm where a small doctor model steers a frozen patient LLM via token-level flow-guided preference optimization.

entry.title: Investigating Tool-Memory Conflicts in Tool-Augmented LLMs

author.name: Jiali Cheng, Rui Pan, Hadi Amiri

entry.summary: Identifies Tool-Memory Conflict (TMC), a new type of knowledge conflict where LLM parametric knowledge contradicts external tool knowledge. Finds existing conflict resolution techniques are ineffective.

entry.title: V-Zero: Self-Improving Multimodal Reasoning with Zero Annotation

author.name: Han Wang, Yi Yang, Jingyuan Hu, Minfeng Zhu, Wei Chen

entry.summary: Introduces V-Zero, a post-training framework for VLM self-improvement using only unlabeled images. Creates co-evolutionary loop between Questioner and Solver roles with dual-track reasoning reward.

entry.title: Projected Microbatch Accumulation yields reference-free proximal policy updates for reinforcement learning

author.name: Nilin Abrahamsen

entry.summary: Introduces PROMA, a proximal policy update method for LLM fine-tuning that projects out gradient components during backward pass, enabling tighter KL divergence control without reference policies or likelihood-ratio clipping.

entry.title: Representation-Aware Unlearning via Activation Signatures: From Suppression to Knowledge-Signature Erasure

author.name: Syed Naveed Mahmood, Md. Rezaur Rahman Bhuiyan, Tasfia Zaman, Jareen Tasneem Khondaker, Md. Sameer Sakib, Nazia Tasnim, Farig Sadeque

entry.summary: Knowledge Immunization Framework (KIF) addresses LLM unlearning by targeting internal activation signatures rather than surface outputs, achieving near-oracle erasure (FQ≈0.99) for GDPR compliance and model safety.

entry.title: See Less, Drive Better: Generalizable End-to-End Autonomous Driving via Foundation Models Stochastic Patch Selection

author.name: Amir Mallak, Erfan Aasi, Shiva Sreeram, Tsun-Hsuan Wang, Daniela Rus, Alaa Maalouf

entry.summary: MIT/Daniela Rus team shows foundation model patch features are highly redundant (90% variance in 17/64 components) and proposes stochastic patch selection to improve autonomous driving OOD generalization.

entry.title: Skill-Aware Data Selection and Fine-Tuning for Data-Efficient Reasoning Distillation

author.name: Lechen Zhang, Yunxiang Zhang, Wei Hu, Lu Wang

entry.summary: Skill-centric reasoning distillation framework selects training data targeting student's weak skills. With only 1,000 examples from 100K corpus, surpasses random sampling while improving skill decomposition.

entry.title: Be Your Own Red Teamer: Safety Alignment via Self-Play and Reflective Experience Replay

author.name: Hao Wang, Yanting Wang, Hao Li, Rui Li, Lei Sha

entry.summary: Safety Self-Play (SSP) enables LLM to be its own red teamer, acting as both attacker generating jailbreaks and defender, achieving autonomous evolving adversarial capabilities.

entry.title: Action100M: A Large-scale Video Action Dataset

author.name: Delong Chen, Tejaswi Kasarla, Yejin Bang, Mustafa Shukor, Willy Chung, Jade Yu, Allen Bolourchi, Theo Moutakanni, Pascale Fung

entry.summary: Introduces Action100M, a massive dataset with ~100 million temporally localized video segments from 1.2M instructional videos (14.6 years), generated automatically using V-JEPA 2 embeddings and reasoning models.

entry.title: Test your interpretability techniques by de-censoring Chinese models

author.name: Khoi Tran

entry.summary: Proposes using Chinese censored models as 'model organisms' for testing interpretability techniques. Shows these models know censored information but refuse/lie, making them natural targets for secret extraction research.

entry.title: Evidence-Augmented Policy Optimization with Reward Co-Evolution for Long-Context Reasoning

author.name: Xin Guan, Zijian Li, Shen Huang, Pengjun Xie, Jingren Zhou, Jiuxin Cao

entry.summary: Introduces EAPO (Evidence-Augmented Policy Optimization) for long-context reasoning, providing dense process supervision via Group-Relative Evidence Reward. Validates that evidence extraction is the decisive bottleneck.

entry.title: Closing the Data Loop: Using OpenDataArena to Engineer Superior Training Datasets

author.name: Xin Gao, Xiaoyang Wang, Yun Zhu, Mengzhang Cai, Conghui He, Lijun Wu

entry.summary: Proposes closed-loop dataset engineering using OpenDataArena to transform benchmarking into feedback for dataset construction. Introduces ODA-Math-460k with novel two-step curation methodology.

entry.title: Beyond Rule-Based Workflows: An Information-Flow-Orchestrated Multi-Agents Paradigm via Agent-to-Agent Communication from CORAL

author.name: Xinxing Ren, Quagmire Zang, Caelum Forder, Suman Deb, Ahsen Tahir, Roman J. Georgio, Peter Carroll, Zekun Guo

entry.summary: Introduces CORAL, an information-flow-orchestrated multi-agent paradigm that replaces predefined workflows with dynamic agent-to-agent communication. A dedicated orchestrator monitors progress and dynamically routes information based on task state.

entry.title: Bounded Hyperbolic Tangent: A Stable and Efficient Alternative to Pre-Layer Normalization in Large Language Models

author.name: Hoyoon Byun, Youngjun Choi, Taero Kim, Sungrae Park, Kyungwoo Song

entry.summary: Proposes Bounded Hyperbolic Tangent (BHyT) as drop-in replacement for Pre-Layer Normalization, addressing efficiency and depth-related instability. Couples tanh nonlinearity with explicit input bounding.

entry.title: MedRedFlag: Investigating how LLMs Redirect Misconceptions in Real-World Health Communication

author.name: Sraavya Sambara, Yuan Pu, Ayman Ali, Vishala Mishra, Lionel Wong, Monica Agrawal

entry.summary: Investigates how LLMs handle health questions containing false premises, introducing MedRedFlag benchmark of 1100+ Reddit questions requiring redirection. Finds LLMs often fail at this crucial medical communication skill.

entry.title: LOOKAT: Lookup-Optimized Key-Attention for Memory-Efficient Transformers

author.name: Aryan Karmore

entry.summary: Proposes LOOKAT using product quantization and lookup tables for KV cache compression, transforming attention from memory-bound to compute-bound by applying vector database compression techniques.

entry.title: Fundamental Limitations of Favorable Privacy-Utility Guarantees for DP-SGD

author.name: Murat Bilgehan Ertan, Marten van Dijk

entry.summary: Analyzes DP-SGD in f-differential privacy framework, deriving explicit bounds on achievable trade-off curves showing fundamental limitations on privacy-utility guarantees under shuffled sampling.

entry.title: STEM: Scaling Transformers with Embedding Modules

author.name: Ranajoy Sadhukhan, Sheng Cao, Harry Dong, Changsheng Zhao, Attiano Purpura-Pontoniere, Yuandong Tian, Zechun Liu, Beidi Chen

entry.summary: Introduces STEM, replacing FFN up-projection with layer-local embedding lookup for static token-indexed sparsity, enabling CPU offload and reducing FLOPs while improving performance over dense baselines.

entry.title: Patient-Similarity Cohort Reasoning in Clinical Text-to-SQL

author.name: Yifei Shen, Yilun Zhao, Justice Ou, Tinglin Huang, Arman Cohan

entry.summary: CLINSQL benchmark of 633 expert-annotated clinical text-to-SQL tasks on MIMIC-IV requiring multi-table joins and patient-similarity reasoning. Evaluates 22 models showing significant gap from clinical deployment.

entry.title: The Assistant Axis: Situating and Stabilizing the Default Persona of Language Models

author.name: Christina Lu, Jack Gallagher, Jonathan Michala, Kyle Fish, Jack Lindsey

entry.summary: Discovers 'Assistant Axis' as leading component of LLM persona space across models. Steering along this axis controls helpful/harmless behavior vs tendency to identify as other entities.

entry.title: Topo-RAG: Topology-aware retrieval for hybrid text-table documents

author.name: Alex Dantart, Marco K\'ovacs-Navarro

entry.title: Research Summary: January 15, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research centers on AI security frameworks and alignment challenges in reasoning models. Bruce Schneier introduces Promptware, reconceptualizing prompt injection as a distinct malware class with a five-step kill chain model. OpenAI's alignment team presents Confessions research for detecting reward-hacked outputs.

  • A.X K1 debuts as a 519B MoE model with Think-Fusion enabling user-controllable reasoning depth
  • DeliberationBench reveals a striking negative result: simple best-single selection achieves 82.5% win rate over multi-LLM deliberation
  • GIFT addresses SFT-RL mismatch in reasoning training via finite-temperature Gibbs initialization
  • Resisting Correction shows RLHF creates resistance to external safety signals, dropping Spearman correlation significantly

Survey work includes The AI Hippocampus organizing LLM memory into implicit, explicit, and agentic paradigms, while Adversarial Tales exposes jailbreak vulnerabilities through cultural narrative framing. DASD-4B-Thinking achieves SOTA reasoning among 4B open-source models through distribution-aligned distillation.

author.name: Shuo Zhang, Chaofa Yuan, Ryan Guo, Xiaomin Yu, Rui Xu, Zhangquan Chen, Zinuo Li, Zhi Yang, Shuhao Guan, Zhenheng Tang, Sen Hu, Liwen Zhang, Ronghao Chen, Huacan Wang

entry.title: A Marketplace for AI-Generated Adult Content and Deepfakes

author.name: Shalmoli Ghosh, Matthew R. DeVerna, Filippo Menczer

entry.title: Layer-Parallel Training for Transformers

entry.title: Hidden States as Early Signals: Step-level Trace Evaluation and Pruning for Efficient Test-Time Scaling

author.name: Zhixiang Liang, Beichen Huang, Zheng Wang, Minjia Zhang

entry.title: STEP3-VL-10B Technical Report

entry.summary: Presents STEP3-VL-10B, a 10B open-source multimodal foundation model trained on 1.2T tokens with unified unfrozen pre-training and Parallel Coordinated Reasoning for test-time compute scaling.

entry.title: Omni-R1: Towards the Unified Generative Paradigm for Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Dongjie Cheng, Yongqi Li, Zhixin Ma, Hongru Cai, Yupeng Hu, Wenjie Wang, Liqiang Nie, Wenjie Li

entry.summary: Omni-R1 proposes unified generative multimodal reasoning that generates intermediate images during reasoning, enabling diverse reasoning skills like zooming or marking within a single paradigm.

entry.title: Private LLM Inference on Consumer Blackwell GPUs: A Practical Guide for Cost-Effective Local Deployment in SMEs

author.name: Jonathan Knoop, Hendrik Holtmann

entry.summary: Systematic evaluation of NVIDIA Blackwell consumer GPUs (RTX 5060 Ti, 5070 Ti, 5090) for production LLM inference across multiple models, quantization formats, and workloads including RAG and multi-LoRA serving.

entry.title: Efficient Paths and Dense Rewards: Probabilistic Flow Reasoning for Large Language Models

author.name: Yan Liu, Feng Zhang, Zhanyu Ma, Jun Xu, Jiuchong Gao, Jinghua Hao, Renqing He, Han Liu, Yangdong Deng

entry.summary: CoT-Flow reconceptualizes chain-of-thought reasoning as continuous probabilistic flow, enabling quantification of each step's contribution toward the answer. Addresses inference inefficiency and sparse supervision limitations.

entry.title: TAG-MoE: Task-Aware Gating for Unified Generative Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Yu Xu, Hongbin Yan, Juan Cao, Yiji Cheng, Tiankai Hang, Runze He, Zijin Yin, Shiyi Zhang, Yuxin Zhang, Jintao Li, Chunyu Wang, Qinglin Lu, Tong-Yee Lee, Fan Tang

entry.title: Blue Teaming Function-Calling Agents

author.name: Greta Dolcetti, Giulio Zizzo, Sergio Maffeis

entry.summary: Experimental evaluation assessing robustness of four open-source LLMs with function-calling capabilities against three attacks, measuring effectiveness of eight defenses. Finds models are not safe by default.

entry.title: AI Safety at the Frontier: Paper Highlights of December 2025

author.name: gasteigerjo

entry.summary: Comprehensive summary of December 2025 AI safety papers highlighting sandbagging detection challenges, alignment faking research, frontier cyber capabilities crossing expert thresholds, and mitigation techniques like recontextualization.

entry.title: M$^3$Searcher: Modular Multimodal Information Seeking Agency with Retrieval-Oriented Reasoning

author.name: Xiaohan Yu, Chao Feng, Lang Mei, Chong Chen

entry.summary: M³Searcher extends DeepResearch-style agents to multimodal settings by decoupling information acquisition from answer derivation, addressing training data scarcity for multi-step multimodal search.

entry.title: RIFT: Repurposing Negative Samples via Reward-Informed Fine-Tuning

author.name: Zehua Liu, Shuqi Liu, Tao Zhong, Mingxuan Yuan

entry.summary: Proposes RIFT (Reward Informed Fine-Tuning), which repurposes rejected samples in RFT by reweighting losses with scalar rewards rather than discarding them, with stabilized loss formulation to prevent training collapse.

entry.title: RISER: Orchestrating Latent Reasoning Skills for Adaptive Activation Steering

author.name: Wencheng Ye, Liang Peng, Xiaoyang Yuan, Yi Bin, Pengpeng Zeng, Hengyu Jin, Heng Tao Shen

entry.summary: RISER uses a router-based framework to dynamically compose reasoning vectors from a library, steering LLM reasoning in activation space without parameter updates via reinforcement learning optimization.

entry.title: Scalable and Reliable Evaluation of AI Knowledge Retrieval Systems: RIKER and the Coherent Simulated Universe

author.name: JV Roig

entry.summary: RIKER introduces paradigm inversion for knowledge evaluation - generating documents from known ground truth rather than extracting truth from documents. Evaluates 33 models using 21B+ tokens.

entry.title: Where Knowledge Collides: A Mechanistic Study of Intra-Memory Knowledge Conflict in Language Models

author.name: Minh Vu Pham, Hsuvas Borkakoty, Yufang Hou

entry.summary: Mechanistic interpretability study of intra-memory knowledge conflict in LMs, using framework to identify where and how conflicting pre-training knowledge is encoded within internal representations.

entry.title: Fast-ThinkAct: Efficient Vision-Language-Action Reasoning via Verbalizable Latent Planning

author.name: Chi-Pin Huang, Yunze Man, Zhiding Yu, Min-Hung Chen, Jan Kautz, Yu-Chiang Frank Wang, Fu-En Yang

entry.summary: Proposes Fast-ThinkAct for efficient Vision-Language-Action reasoning via verbalizable latent planning, distilling from teacher with preference-guided objective to achieve compact planning without lengthy explicit CoT traces.

entry.title: Video-MSR: Benchmarking Multi-hop Spatial Reasoning Capabilities of MLLMs

author.name: Rui Zhu, Xin Shen, Shuchen Wu, Chenxi Miao, Xin Yu, Yang Li, Weikang Li, Deguo Xia, Jizhou Huang

entry.summary: Introduces Video-MSR, first benchmark for multi-hop spatial reasoning in videos with four tasks: Constrained Localization, Chain-based Reference Retrieval, Route Planning, and Counterfactual Deduction.

entry.title: ART: Action-based Reasoning Task Benchmarking for Medical AI Agents

author.name: Ananya Mantravadi, Shivali Dalmia, Abhishek Mukherji

entry.summary: Presents ART, a benchmark for evaluating medical AI agents on action-based reasoning tasks involving threshold evaluation, temporal aggregation, and conditional logic over EHRs. Identifies three dominant error categories in existing benchmarks.

entry.title: What Do LLM Agents Know About Their World? Task2Quiz: A Paradigm for Studying Environment Understanding

author.name: Siyuan Liu, Hongbang Yuan, Xinze Li, Ziyue Zhu, Yixin Cao, Yu-Gang Jiang

entry.title: ProFit: Leveraging High-Value Signals in SFT via Probability-Guided Token Selection

author.name: Tao Liu, Taiqiang Wu, Runming Yang, Shaoning Sun, Junjie Wang, Yujiu Yang

entry.title: SimMerge: Learning to Select Merge Operators from Similarity Signals

entry.summary: Introduces SimMerge, a predictive method for selecting best model merge using task-agnostic similarity signals between models, avoiding expensive merge-and-evaluate searches.

entry.title: How Many Human Judgments Are Enough? Feasibility Limits of Human Preference Evaluation

author.name: Wilson Y. Lee

entry.title: DeepResearchEval: An Automated Framework for Deep Research Task Construction and Agentic Evaluation

entry.title: V-DPM: 4D Video Reconstruction with Dynamic Point Maps

author.name: Qinglong Shi, Donghai Wang, Hantao Zhou, Jiguo Li, Jun Xu, Jiuchong Gao, Jinghua Hao, Renqing He

entry.title: Collaborative Multi-Agent Test-Time Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning

author.name: Zhiyuan Hu, Yunhai Hu, Juncheng Liu, Shuyue Stella Li, Yucheng Wang, Zhen Xu, See-Kiong Ng, Anh Tuan Luu, Xinxing Xu, Bryan Hooi, Cynthia Breazeal, Hae Won Park

entry.title: ForensicFormer: Hierarchical Multi-Scale Reasoning for Cross-Domain Image Forgery Detection

author.name: Hema Hariharan Samson

entry.title: Ability Transfer and Recovery via Modularized Parameters Localization

entry.title: SLAM-LLM: A Modular, Open-Source Multimodal Large Language Model Framework and Best Practice for Speech, Language, Audio and Music Processing

author.name: Ziyang Ma, Guanrou Yang, Wenxi Chen, Zhifu Gao, Yexing Du, Xiquan Li, Zhisheng Zheng, Haina Zhu, Jianheng Zhuo, Zheshu Song, Ruiyang Xu, Tiranrui Wang, Yifan Yang, Yanqiao Zhu, Zhikang Niu, Liumeng Xue, Yinghao Ma, Ruibin Yuan, Shiliang Zhang, Kai Yu, Eng Siong Chng, Xie Chen

entry.title: Programming over Thinking: Efficient and Robust Multi-Constraint Planning

author.name: Derrick Goh Xin Deik, Quanyu Long, Zhengyuan Liu, Nancy F. Chen, Wenya Wang

entry.title: Imagine-then-Plan: Agent Learning from Adaptive Lookahead with World Models

author.name: Youwei Liu, Jian Wang, Hanlin Wang, Beichen Guo, Wenjie Li

author.name: Jiaxi Li, Yue Zhu, Eun Kyung Lee, Klara Nahrstedt

entry.title: Navigating Ideation Space: Decomposed Conceptual Representations for Positioning Scientific Ideas

author.name: Yuexi Shen, Minqian Liu, Dawei Zhou, Lifu Huang

entry.title: SubTokenTest: A Practical Benchmark for Real-World Sub-token Understanding

author.name: Shuyang Hou, Yi Hu, Muhan Zhang

author.name: Tianyi Niu, Justin Chih-Yao Chen, Genta Indra Winata, Shi-Xiong Zhang, Supriyo Chakraborty, Sambit Sahu, Yue Zhang, Elias Stengel-Eskin, Mohit Bansal

entry.title: PhyRPR: Training-Free Physics-Constrained Video Generation

author.name: Yibo Zhao, Hengjia Li, Xiaofei He, Boxi Wu

entry.title: GaussianFluent: Gaussian Simulation for Dynamic Scenes with Mixed Materials

author.name: Bei Huang, Yixin Chen, Ruijie Lu, Gang Zeng, Hongbin Zha, Yuru Pei, Siyuan Huang

entry.title: Reading or Reasoning? Format Decoupled Reinforcement Learning for Document OCR

entry.title: Bias Dynamics in BabyLMs: Towards a Compute-Efficient Sandbox for Democratising Pre-Training Debiasing

entry.title: Value-Aware Numerical Representations for Transformer Language Models

author.name: Andreea Dutulescu, Stefan Ruseti, Mihai Dascalu

entry.title: MAXS: Meta-Adaptive Exploration with LLM Agents

author.name: Jian Zhang, Zhiyuan Wang, Zhangqi Wang, Yu He, Haoran Luo, li yuan, Lingling Zhang, Rui Mao, Qika Lin, Jun Liu

entry.title: Consistency-Aware Editing for Entity-level Unlearning in Language Models

author.name: Xiaoqi Han, V\'ictor Guti\'errez-Basulto, Ru Li, Xiaoli Li, Jiye Liang, Jeff Z. Pan

entry.summary: Proposes consistency-aware model editing for entity-level unlearning in LLMs, addressing the need to remove all knowledge of specific entities rather than just individual facts.

entry.title: Fairness risk and its privacy-enabled solution in AI-driven robotic applications

author.name: Le Liu, Bangguo Yu, Nynke Vellinga, Ming Cao

entry.summary: Proposes utility-aware fairness metrics for robotic decision-making and analyzes fairness jointly with privacy, deriving conditions under which privacy budgets govern fairness.

entry.title: Proactively Detecting Threats: A Novel Approach Using LLMs

author.name: Aniesh Chawla, Udbhav Prasad

entry.summary: First systematic evaluation of LLMs for proactively identifying indicators of compromise from unstructured threat intelligence, achieving 0.958 precision with Gemini 1.5 Pro.

entry.title: Understanding or Memorizing? A Case Study of German Definite Articles in Language Models

author.name: Jonathan Drechsel, Erisa Bytyqi, Steffen Herbold

entry.title: Learning Whole-Body Human-Humanoid Interaction from Human-Human Demonstrations

author.name: Wei-Jin Huang, Yue-Yi Zhang, Yi-Lin Wei, Zhi-Wei Xia, Juantao Tan, Yuan-Ming Li, Zhilin Zhao, Wei-Shi Zheng

entry.title: Geometric Stability: The Missing Axis of Representations

entry.title: LatencyPrism: Online Non-intrusive Latency Sculpting for SLO-Guaranteed LLM Inference

author.name: Du Yin, Jiayi Ren, Xiayu Sun, Tianyao Zhou, Haizhu Zhou, Ruiyan Ma, Danyang Zhang

entry.title: When to Trust: A Causality-Aware Calibration Framework for Accurate Knowledge Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Jing Ren, Bowen Li, Ziqi Xu, Xinkun Zhang, Haytham Fayek, Xiaodong Li

entry.summary: Proposes Ca2KG for causality-aware calibration of Knowledge Graph RAG systems that are often severely overconfident. Uses counterfactual prompting to expose retrieval-dependent uncertainties.

entry.title: The Semantic Lifecycle in Embodied AI: Acquisition, Representation and Storage via Foundation Models

author.name: Shuai Chen, Hao Chen, Yuanchen Bei, Tianyang Zhao, Zhibo Zhou, Feiran Huang

entry.summary: Surveys semantic information lifecycle in embodied AI through foundation models, covering acquisition, representation, and storage of multi-source, multi-stage semantic information.

entry.title: Pairing-free Group-level Knowledge Distillation for Robust Gastrointestinal Lesion Classification in White-Light Endoscopy

author.name: Qiang Hu, Qimei Wang, Yingjie Guo, Qiang Li, Zhiwei Wang

entry.summary: Introduces PaGKD, a pairing-free group-level knowledge distillation framework enabling cross-modal learning between WLI and NBI endoscopy without requiring paired images.

entry.title: Affostruction: 3D Affordance Grounding with Generative Reconstruction

author.name: Chunghyun Park, Seunghyeon Lee, Minsu Cho

entry.summary: Proposes Affostruction for affordance grounding from RGBD images, using generative reconstruction to predict affordances on complete geometry including unobserved regions.

entry.title: MAD: Motion Appearance Decoupling for efficient Driving World Models

author.name: Ahmad Rahimi, Valentin Gerard, Eloi Zablocki, Matthieu Cord, Alexandre Alahi

entry.summary: Proposes MAD, an efficient adaptation framework converting video diffusion models to controllable driving world models by decoupling motion learning from appearance synthesis.

entry.title: OpenVoxel: Training-Free Grouping and Captioning Voxels for Open-Vocabulary 3D Scene Understanding

author.name: Sheng-Yu Huang, Jaesung Choe, Yu-Chiang Frank Wang, Cheng Sun

entry.title: Image2Garment: Simulation-ready Garment Generation from a Single Image

entry.title: Efficient Camera-Controlled Video Generation of Static Scenes via Sparse Diffusion and 3D Rendering

author.name: Jieying Chen, Jeffrey Hu, Joan Lasenby, Ayush Tewari

entry.summary: Proposes efficient camera-controlled video generation using sparse diffusion for keyframes combined with 3D reconstruction and rendering for intermediate views.

entry.title: CrowdLLM: Building LLM-Based Digital Populations Augmented with Generative Models

author.name: Ryan Feng Lin, Keyu Tian, Hanming Zheng, Congjing Zhang, Li Zeng, Shuai Huang

entry.summary: CrowdLLM integrates LLMs with generative models to create digital populations that better capture the accuracy and diversity of real human populations for simulation and research.

entry.title: AI Deployment Authorisation: A Global Standard for Machine-Readable Governance of High-Risk Artificial Intelligence

author.name: Daniel Djan Saparning

entry.summary: Introduces ADAS, a machine-readable regulatory framework producing cryptographically verifiable deployment certificates based on risk, alignment, externality, control, and auditability dimensions.

entry.title: OpenDecoder: Open Large Language Model Decoding to Incorporate Document Quality in RAG

author.name: Fengran Mo, Zhan Su, Yuchen Hui, Jinghan Zhang, Jia Ao Sun, Zheyuan Liu, Chao Zhang, Tetsuya Sakai, Jian-Yun Nie

author.name: Jean Feng, Avni Kothari, Patrick Vossler, Andrew Bishara, Lucas Zier, Newton Addo, Aaron Kornblith, Yan Shuo Tan, Chandan Singh

entry.title: Position on LLM-Assisted Peer Review: Addressing Reviewer Gap through Mentoring and Feedback

author.name: JungMin Yun, JuneHyoung Kwon, MiHyeon Kim, YoungBin Kim

entry.summary: Position paper arguing against LLMs automatically generating peer reviews, instead proposing LLM-assisted mentoring and feedback systems to develop reviewer competencies and improve review quality.

entry.title: Informed Consent for AI Consciousness Research: A Talmudic Framework for Graduated Protections

author.name: Ira Wolfson

entry.summary: Proposes a Talmudic framework for graduated protections in AI consciousness research, addressing how to ethically conduct experiments on systems whose moral status is uncertain.

entry.title: Learning Domain-Invariant Representations for Cross-Domain Image Registration via Scene-Appearance Disentanglement

author.name: Jiahao Qin, Yiwen Wang

entry.summary: SAR-Net decomposes images into domain-invariant scene representations and domain-specific appearance codes, enabling cross-domain image registration through re-rendering rather than direct matching.

entry.title: From Symbolic to Natural-Language Relations: Rethinking Knowledge Graph Construction in the Era of Large Language Models

author.name: Kanyao Han, Yushang Lai

entry.summary: Proposes rethinking knowledge graph construction by using natural-language relations instead of predefined symbolic schemas, arguing that LLMs enable new paradigms where contextual, nuanced relations can replace discrete categorical labels.

entry.title: Reward Learning through Ranking Mean Squared Error

author.name: Chaitanya Kharyal, Calarina Muslimani, Matthew E. Taylor

entry.summary: Introduces R4 (Ranked Return Regression for RL), a reward learning method using novel ranking mean squared error (rMSE) loss that treats human ratings as ordinal targets, enabling learning from trajectory-rating pairs.

entry.title: On the Hardness of Computing Counterfactual and Semifactual Explanations in XAI

author.name: Andr\'e Artelt, Martin Olsen, Kevin Tierney

entry.summary: Proves computational hardness and inapproximability results for generating counterfactual and semifactual explanations, strengthening the argument that XAI explanations are often hard to both compute and approximate.

entry.title: DPWriter: Reinforcement Learning with Diverse Planning Branching for Creative Writing

author.name: Qian Cao, Yahui Liu, Wei Bi, Yi Zhao, Ruihua Song, Xiting Wang, Ruiming Tang, Guorui Zhou, Han Li

entry.summary: Proposes DPWriter, an RL framework for creative writing with semi-structured long Chain-of-Thought and Diverse Planning Branching that introduces strategic divergence at planning phase to address diversity collapse.

entry.title: Interpretable Probability Estimation with LLMs via Shapley Reconstruction

author.name: Yang Nan, Qihao Wen, Jiahao Wang, Pengfei He, Ravi Tandon, Yong Ge, Han Xu

entry.summary: Proposes PRISM, a framework using Shapley values to decompose LLM probability predictions into interpretable contributions from input facts. Addresses both transparency and precision challenges in LLM-based probability estimation.

entry.title: $D^2Prune$: Sparsifying Large Language Models via Dual Taylor Expansion and Attention Distribution Awareness

author.name: Lang Xiong, Ning Liu, Ao Ren, Yuheng Bai, Haining Fang, BinYan Zhang, Zhe Jiang, Yujuan Tan, Duo Liu

entry.title: Parallelizable memory recurrent units

author.name: Florent De Geeter, Gaspard Lambrechts, Damien Ernst, Guillaume Drion

entry.summary: Proposes parallelizable memory recurrent units that maintain nonlinear dynamics while enabling parallel training. Addresses efficiency gap between Transformers (parallel but slow generation) and SSMs (fast but linearized).

entry.title: Exploring Fine-Tuning for Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Aditya Tanna, Pratinav Seth, Mohamed Bouadi, Vinay Kumar Sankarapu

entry.summary: Presents first comprehensive study of fine-tuning approaches for Tabular Foundation Models across multiple benchmarks. Finds zero-shot often competitive while fine-tuning benefits are model and data-dependent.

entry.title: Horseshoe Mixtures-of-Experts (HS-MoE)

author.name: Nick Polson, Vadim Sokolov

entry.summary: Develops Horseshoe Mixtures-of-Experts with Bayesian adaptive global-local shrinkage for sparse expert selection. Proposes particle learning algorithm for sequential inference with sufficient statistics tracking.

entry.title: Entropy Sentinel: Continuous LLM Accuracy Monitoring from Decoding Entropy Traces in STEM

author.name: Pedro Memoli Buffa, Luciano Del Corro

entry.title: Beyond Consensus: Perspectivist Modeling and Evaluation of Annotator Disagreement in NLP

author.name: Yinuo Xu, David Jurgens

entry.title: Identity-Robust Language Model Generation via Content Integrity Preservation

entry.title: Research Summary: January 14, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research features a fundamental theoretical breakthrough and significant RLHF/alignment advances. Universal Computation in LM Decoding proves autoregressive decoding alone enables simulation of any algorithm—reshaping capability understanding. Ministral 3 from Mistral delivers efficient 3B/8B/14B models with pretrained, instruction-tuned, and reasoning variants.

Key RLHF methodology findings:

  • GRPO bias systematically underestimates advantages for hard prompts, affecting widely-deployed alignment pipelines
  • On-policy DPO achieves exponential convergence via coverage improvement principle
  • Asymptotic Universal Alignment provides rigorous mathematical framework for test-time scaling guarantees

Safety research reveals critical insights:

  • Surgical Refusal Ablation disentangles refusal from capabilities via concept-guided spectral cleaning
  • ValAct-15k shows LLMs exhibit convergent moral judgments but divergent actions—key alignment gap
  • Sandbagging detection via consistency checks addresses evaluation gaming
  • RAVEN exposes watermark vulnerability through novel view synthesis, threatening content authentication

Reasoning Beyond Chain-of-Thought identifies causal latent features using Sparse Autoencoders, enabling targeted reasoning improvements through feature steering.
